lead_profile_text: Existing home switching to short-term let - owner relocating to Norfolk for a new job, keeping the Leicester house
stl_goal: At least £1,500 per month net to cover the mortgage and costs
property_situation: 3-bed house the lead currently lives in; moving to Norfolk (smaller apartment) so the house will be vacant, furnished and not sold. Mortgaged (Monday deck wrongly says no mortgage). Renovated room by room - most done, some rooms still to finish. Log burner, small veg garden, a 1x1m utility room and loft/shed to be locked off. Move date depends on employer confirmation (mid-October to early November) plus a one-month notice period, so likely December.
primary_blocker: Externally gated by employer confirmation for the Norfolk job and notice period (go-live realistically December); wife is a co-decision-maker; unfinished rooms; scepticism about Leicester demand

meeting_flow.opening_phrase: I thought I'd start just by understanding a bit on your current sort of situation. I understand you're looking at buying a property in Leicester, is that right?
meeting_flow.pivot_to_business: All right then, well, what we'll do is I can go through the figures and we can go through our service, see if it lines up with what you're looking for.
meeting_flow.income_intro: About £33,000 gross per year, and about £2,800 per month ... that's sort of £18,000 per year, about £1,500 per month. £130, £140 nightly rate with 65% occupancy.
meeting_flow.how_it_works_transition: Well, I can go through a bit more on what the service covers so you've got more of an overview of everything.
meeting_flow.pre_close_setup: It sounds to me like it's mostly ready. The only things we're going to be needing to do is like a key safe ... 2 key safes ... have a cleaner go around and have a look ... get some photos taken.
meeting_flow.close_phrase: Is there anything, any concerns or anything else you want to go through, or sort of happy?
meeting_flow.meeting_2_ask: Obviously send me back them photos. If you don't hear from me, I'll get back in touch around sort of late November, December time.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: We would like to get at least $1,500 per month, if we can. Because then that would cover a lot of the costs with mortgages and things like that.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Explained gross vs net: platform commission 15%, cleaning about 18% of gross, management 15% plus VAT - only mortgage and bills remain.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Yeah, this amount of money is exactly more or less what we're looking for.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Everyone thinks like, oh well, Leicester, who is going to Leicester? Who is going to use Airbnb in Leicester? And with your experience, what could you say to me about this?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Every area has leisure demand; competitor operators nearby are a good sign; comparables drive the numbers. Admitted the 'who books' slide wrongly showed Manchester data.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Let's say that one month no one comes, I still have the payments to do ... with the platform or with the cleaning?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: No - costs are a percentage of revenue; the only fixed costs are mortgage and bills.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Another thing is damage ... damage of the property or damage of something in the property. How does that work?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: £250-£400 security deposit per guest, ID check before check-in details, 2-3 night minimum stays, and platform insurance for major incidents.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: We have a log burner ... could there work something like they provide the first amount of wood and you buy more if you need more? ... wouldn't that be an advantage or a good feature to have?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: I would probably avoid the log burner thing altogether - fire hazard and no competitive benefit; guests would sooner turn the heating up; parking, EV charger, workspace and pet-friendly are stronger amenities.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: But then if they just go out and get some wood ... how can I protect myself?

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Do you guys ask before deciding to do some maintenance on the house, or is it more like a decision?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: We go ahead up to £300 a month (one job or accumulated), above that we get approval; low-risk jobs batched into a day rate, major ones on call-out; cleaner inspects after every stay, thorough inspection 2-3 times a year.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Is it possible that I lock a place in the house, for example the loft or even the shed? ... a very small utility room, literally 1 by 1 meter.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Loft, shed and a small utility room are fine; blocking a whole bedroom would mean listing it as 2 bedrooms.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: How does that work in a way of contract? ... 6 months, 1 year, 1 year and a half, or every month just renew itself?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: 6-month fixed term, then a 3-month notice term, mainly to service booked guests before releasing the property.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Could you guys help out ... providing someone, even if I pay, to finish off the job or to do a little maintenance? ... Is garden maintenance included?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Send photos on WhatsApp and I can give recommendations; garden maintenance is included on an ad hoc basis with a contact list of gardeners; free setup guide in the action plan.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Okay. Sounds good. I think I asked every question that I had in mind. I'll send you the photos.

zac_language.numbers_framing: Gross about £33,000 to net about £18,000 (£1,500/month) after 15% platform, ~18% cleaning, 15% + VAT management; low case £800, high case £2,200; slow months March, September, October
zac_language.objection_handling_pattern: Direct and probability-based ('very unlikely', 'never heard of a guest do that') plus process detail (deposit, ID check, £300 maintenance limit); less effective when the lead wanted reassurance on the log burner

what_they_needed_most: A way to cover mortgage costs while away
what_fell_flat: Dismissing the log burner as a feature
profile_psychology_intersection.recommended_meeting_adjustment: For relocating owners, confirm their situation up front, have location-specific demand data ready, give concrete protections for any special features and plan the follow-up around their move date and their partner's input
